USE THIS MODEL

Settings reference (format v1)

Use This Model shows three cards: Chatting (chat), Everyday Coding (code) and Crazy Hard Coding (crazy). For each one it recommends the cheapest model whose score is at least your minimum and whose input price is at most your maximum. There is no database and no account: every setting lives in the URL, so a link is the whole configuration. Save it, share it, or put it behind your own short link.

Parameters

Each category takes the same parameters, prefixed with its name. Replace chat with code or crazy.

ParamRequiredFormatMeaning
vno1Settings format version. Omitted means 1. A future breaking change ships as v=2; v1 links keep working.
chatyeskey[:weight],...Benchmarks to score with, and their relative weights (default weight 1). chat=eci, chat=eci:2,aai:1.
chat_maxyesnumber ≥ 0Max input price in USD per 1M tokens. chat_max=1.5
chat_minyes0-100Min combined score (normalized scale, see below). chat_min=70
chat_missnoexclude | reweight | zeroWhat to do when a model has no score on a chosen benchmark. Default exclude.
chat_covno0-100Only with reweight: minimum % of the chosen weight a model must have scores for.
chat_locknoOpenRouter model idLocks the card to exactly this model (see Locked links). chat_lock=openai/gpt-6.1-sol

Unknown parameters, duplicated parameters, or invalid values make the link invalid: the page lists exactly what is wrong and the bot endpoint returns HTTP 400. Parameters starting with utm_ are ignored so marketing tags never break a link.

Benchmarks

KeyBenchmarkWhat it measuresModels today
eciEpoch Capabilities Index (ECI)Epoch AI's composite capability score, stitched across dozens of benchmarks with item-response theory. General capability.75
aaiArtificial Analysis Intelligence IndexArtificial Analysis' composite of reasoning, knowledge, math and coding evals. General capability.33
aacArtificial Analysis Coding Agent IndexAgentic coding (DeepSWE, Terminal-Bench, SWE-Atlas QnA) run inside coding-agent harnesses. Best configuration per model.24
daDesign Arena Frontend (Elo)Human-preference Elo for agent-built web apps (rows with 500+ battles).44
vibeVals AI Vibe CodeBuild-an-app-from-a-prompt coding accuracy.72
vcbVals AI VCB 1-100Vals coding benchmark accuracy.24
sweVals AI SWE-bench MultimodalSWE-bench Multimodal accuracy (visual software issues).20

Benchmark keys are permanent. If a source disappears its key stays valid; models just stop having that score, which the missing-data mode handles.

How scores are normalized

Benchmarks use different scales (ECI points, Elo, % accuracy), so every benchmark is rescaled to 0-100 by Use This Model's data refresh, with one fixed method. It is not a setting.

Per benchmark: min-max over published models. score = 100 * (raw - min) / (max - min), rounded to 0.1. Best published model = 100, weakest = 0. A model's raw score is its best published configuration (for example its highest reasoning effort) on that benchmark. Normalization is computed over the models we publish, which are the models we can price.

The combined score for a category is the weighted average of the chosen normalized scores, so single-benchmark and multi-benchmark settings use the same 0-100 scale and a floor of 80 means the same thing either way. Because the scale is relative to the field, a model's score can move when much stronger or weaker models are added; a score of 100 always means "best tracked model on this benchmark today".

Missing data

  • exclude (default): a model must have every chosen benchmark, otherwise it is not ranked.
  • reweight: average only over the benchmarks the model has, re-dividing by their weights. Add _cov to require a minimum share of weight, e.g. code_miss=reweight&code_cov=50.
  • zero: a missing benchmark counts as 0.

In every mode a model with no score on any chosen benchmark is not ranked.

Price

Price is the model's input price in USD per 1M tokens, the OpenRouter list price for that model id. It is one number every provider publishes, so it is comparable across all models. The real cost of a task also depends on output tokens (often several times more expensive per token) and on how verbose or agentic a model is, so two models with the same input price can cost very differently per task. Output price is shown in each model's detail view for reference; filtering and ranking use input price only.

Locked links

Normally picks float: when data changes tomorrow, the same link may recommend a newer model. Add chat_lock, code_lock and/or crazy_lock to pin a card to exactly that model. Use Share Locked Models on the page to build one; you can choose any model per category before copying. A locked card always shows the locked model, even if it is retired from the data. Update your link when you want to move.

Examples

Recommended settings (ECI everywhere):

https://usethismodel.vercel.app/?chat=eci&chat_max=1&chat_min=65&code=eci&code_max=3&code_min=80&crazy=eci&crazy_max=15&crazy_min=95

Coding blend, tolerate missing benchmarks if a model has at least half the weight:

https://usethismodel.vercel.app/?chat=eci&chat_max=1&chat_min=65&code=aac:2,vibe:1,da:1&code_max=3&code_min=70&code_miss=reweight&code_cov=50&crazy=eci,aac&crazy_max=15&crazy_min=90

Same settings with locked models:

https://usethismodel.vercel.app/?chat=eci&chat_max=1&chat_min=65&code=eci&code_max=3&code_min=80&crazy=eci&crazy_max=15&crazy_min=95&chat_lock=openai/gpt-6.1-sol&code_lock=anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5&crazy_lock=anthropic/claude-opus-5.5

Bot endpoint

GET /api/picks takes exactly the same parameters and runs the same calculation code as the page, so bots and humans always get the same picks.

curl 'https://usethismodel.vercel.app/api/picks?chat=eci&chat_max=1&chat_min=65&code=eci&code_max=3&code_min=80&crazy=eci&crazy_max=15&crazy_min=95'

200 response (abridged):

{
  "v": 1,
  "data_updated_utc": "2026-11-11T12:00:00.000Z",
  "url": "https://usethismodel.vercel.app/?chat=eci&chat_max=1&chat_min=65&code=eci&code_max=3&code_min=80&crazy=eci&crazy_max=15&crazy_min=95",
  "categories": {
    "chat": {
      "title": "Chatting",
      "status": "ok",            // ok | no-model-qualifies | locked | locked-model-not-in-data
      "model": { "id": "...", "name": "...", "org": "...",
                 "input_usd_per_1m": 0.1, "output_usd_per_1m": 0.5, "score": 67.8 },
      "qualifying_count": 3,
      "runners_up": [ ... ],
      "settings": { ... }
    },
    "code": { ... }, "crazy": { ... }
  }
}

No parameters, unknown parameters or invalid values return HTTP 400:

{ "error": "invalid_settings",
  "errors": [ { "param": "code_min", "problem": "missing (min score, 0-100)" } ],
  "docs": "https://usethismodel.vercel.app/docs",
  "example": "https://usethismodel.vercel.app/api/picks?chat=eci&chat_max=1&chat_min=65&code=eci&code_max=3&code_min=80&crazy=eci&crazy_max=15&crazy_min=95" }

Raw data for your own math: /models.json (normalized scores, raw scores, input/output $ per 1M, refreshed daily). The calculation module itself is /calc.mjs.
